J_2297.c: Colour woodblock print of the poetry judge Jōsuitei Shitami studying a poem slip by either Katsushika Hokusai or Hishikawa Sōri, Japan, about 1797. Shikishiban format, surimono print with poems signed Jōsuitei Shitami of Kuwaori in Mutsu province, Sōshūrō Kinrachi, Gokyūken Yonendō, Shūchōdō Monoyana and Yomo Utagaki Magao.

J_2298.o: Approved Category 2017/Printed Material/Print/Relief Print/Woodblock print; Object by Function/Documents by function/Surimono
J_2298.c: Colour woodblock print, Woman seated on elephant by Katsushika Taito II, Japan, late 1820s or early 1830s. Shikishiban format, surimono print with poems signed Shōkeisha Chiyohiko of Suruga, Bunryōen Matsukage of Itabana in Kōzue province and Bungensha Tamaru.

J_2299.o: Approved Category 2017/Printed Material/Print/Relief Print/Woodblock print; Object by Function/Documents by function/Surimono
J_2299.c: Colour woodblock print, Carp swimming among waterweeds by Katsushika Taito II, Japan, probably 1832. Shikishiban format, surimono print with poems signed Bunshūrō Tomoyoshi, Bunkarō Kiyomaru and Bunbunsha.

J_2300.o: Approved Category 2017/Printed Material/Print/Relief Print/Woodblock print; Object by Function/Documents by function/Surimono
J_2300.c: Colour woodblock print, Seated woman with bow by Katsushika Taito II, printed in Japan, possibly 1832. Shikishiban format, surimono print with poem signed Shōsōen (Komatsuen) Harundo. The woman depicted may be Kayō Fujin, the consort of Prince Hanzoku in tropical India. Kayō Fujin was the first incarnation of a magic nine-tailed fox who appeared as consort to rulers in India, China and Japan. In Japan, the fox appeared as Tamamo no Mae.

J_2301.o: Approved Category 2017/Printed Material/Print/Relief Print/Woodblock print; Object by Function/Documents by function/Surimono
J_2301.c: Colour woodblock print, Chinese woman playing jabisen by Katsushika Taito II, printed in Japan, probably in 1833. Shikishiban format, surimono print with poem signed Shōsōen (Komatsuen) Harundo.

J_2302.o: Approved Category 2017/Printed Material/Print/Relief Print/Woodblock print; Object by Function/Documents by function/Surimono
J_2302.c: Colour woodblock print, Fifth month from the series 'Five seasonal festivals for the Katsushika group' (Katsushika gosekku) by Katsushika Taito II, printed in Japan, early or mid-1830s. Shikishiban format, surimono print prepared for the Katsushika group with poems signed Bunchien Naomichi and Bunshinsha Hashizumi. The geisha wears the emblem of the Katsushika group. As she rinses out a wine cup, a cuckoo flies overhead. The iris leaves indicate the festival of the fifth month, Tango no sekku.

J_2303.o: Approved Category 2017/Printed Material/Print/Relief Print/Woodblock print; Object by Function/Documents by function/Surimono
J_2303.c: Colour woodblock print, Ninth month from 'Five seasonal festivals for the Katsushika group' (Katsushika gosekku) by Katsushika Taito II , printed in Japan in the early to mid-1830s. Shikishiban format, surimono print prepared for the Katsushika group with poems signed Ogawa Machiami and Bunshōsha Ashichika. Chrysanthemums bloom in the ninth month and so mark the last of the five traditional seasonal festivals.

J_2304.t: Man throwing beans to exorcise demons
J_2304.o: Approved Category 2017/Printed Material/Print/Relief Print/Woodblock print; Object by Function/Documents by function/Egoyomi
J_2304.c: Colour woodblock print, Man throwing beas to exorcise demons by Utagawa Toyoharu, printed in Japan, 1774. Egoyomi (picture calendar) print. Picture calendar print (egoyomi) for the year An’ei 3 (1774). The inscription on the right identifies that the black beans in the sequence indicate long months and the white beans are the short months. During the setsubun festival, beans are thrown to purify the house and cast out demons.

J_2305.t: Woman offering medicinal wine to long-tailed turtle
J_2305.o: Approved Category 2017/Printed Material/Print/Relief Print/Woodblock print; Object by Function/Documents by function/Egoyomi
J_2305.c: Colour woodblock print, Woman offering medicinal wine to long-tailed turtle by Utagawa Toyohiro, printed in Japan, 1796. Picture calendar print (egoyomi) for the year Kansei 8 (1796), a Dragon Year. The character dai (large/long) and numbers for the long months 2, 4, 7, 9, 11 and 12 are written on the dragon-headed water urn.

J_2306.o: Approved Category 2017/Printed Material/Print/Relief Print/Woodblock print; Object by Function/Documents by function/Egoyomi
J_2306.c: Colour woodblock print, Women at Nippori by Utagawa Toyohiro, printed in Japan, 1796. Egoyomi (picture calendar) print. Picture calendar print (egoyomi) for the year Kansei 8 (1796). The characters for the short months are written on the white undersash of the woman on the right and those of the long months are written on the child’s pack. The inscription at the top of the stone monument appears to read 'Nippori', a town outside Edo, noted for the blossoms that could be enjoyed upon Mt Dōkan.

J_2307.t: Standing screen with woman viewing Mt Fuji
J_2307.o: Approved Category 2017/Printed Material/Print/Relief Print/Woodblock print; Object by Function/Documents by function/Surimono
J_2307.c: Colour woodblock print depiction of Standing screen with woman viewing Mt Fuji by Utagawa Toyohiro, printed in Japan, around the mid-1810s. Shikishiban format, surimono print with poems signed Hana no Harundo and Sakuragawa Jihinari.

J_2308.o: Approved Category 2017/Printed Material/Print/Relief Print/Woodblock print; Object by Function/Documents by function/Surimono
J_2308.c: Colour woodblock print, Court carriage by Utagawa Toyohiru, printed in Japan around the mid-1810s. Shikishiban format, surimono print with poems signed Hana no Harundo and Sakuragawa Jihinari.

J_2309.o: Approved Category 2017/Printed Material/Print/Relief Print/Woodblock print; Object by Function/Documents by function/Surimono
J_2309.c: Colour woodblock print, Wine cup and flowering adonis by Utagawa Toyohiro, printed in Japan, possibly 1820. Shikishiban format, surimono print with poems signed Yoshiaki Nakazumi and Sakuragawa Jihinari. The red lacquer sake cup carries a design of a carp climbing a waterfall. If successful in this endeavour the carp will transform into a dragon, like that depicted on the porcelain planter. The choice of subject suggests that this print was created for 1820, a Dragon Year.

J_2310.c: Colour woodblock print, Woman looking at reflection by Utagawa Toyokiyo, printed in Japan around the mid-1810s. The printing is very fine and it is possible that this could be a surimono print with poem trimmed away or a proof impression omitting the text block. The heavy hair ornaments worn by the woman suggest that she is a yūjo working in the brothel district.

J_2311.o: Approved Category 2017/Printed Material/Print/Relief Print/Woodblock print; Object by Function/Documents by function/Surimono
J_2311.c: Colour woodblock print, Actor Ichikawa Ebizō VI by Utagawa Toyokuni, printed in Japan, around the early 1820s. Shikishiban format, surimono print with poems signed Sakuragawa segare Oya no Omokage and Sakuragawa Jihinari. Ebizō VI previously held the name Ichikawa Danjūrō VIII. In this depiction, he is shown in the role of a yakko. Yakko acted as personal servants and agents to Japan's military class. The first poem is written by the son of Sakuragawa Jihinari; the phrase ‘Oya no Omokage’ means ‘His father’s image’.

J_2312.o: Approved Category 2017/Printed Material/Print/Relief Print/Woodblock print; Object by Function/Documents by function/Egoyomi
J_2312.c: Colour woodblock print, Actor performing sanbasō dance by an unknown artist, printed in Japan, 1783. Egoyomi (picture calendar) print. Picture calendar print (egoyomi) for the year Tenmei 3 (1783). The character dai (large/long) and numbers for the long months 2, 4, 5, 7, 9 and 11 are featured on the actor’s clothing. The scene of an old man performing this auspicious dance is featured at the end of the Nō play, Okina.

J_2313.o: Approved Category 2017/Printed Material/Print/Relief Print/Woodblock print; Object by Function/Documents by function/Egoyomi
J_2313.c: Colour woodblock print, Watch with cord and key by an unknown artist, Japan, 1785. Picture calendar print (egoyomi) for the year Tenmei 5 (1785). The character dai (large/long) and numbers for the long months are included on the face of the watch; the numbers of the short months are included in the inscription above.

J_2314.t: Mounter applying backing paper to folding screen
J_2314.o: Approved Category 2017/Printed Material/Print/Relief Print/Woodblock print; Object by Function/Documents by function/Egoyomi
J_2314.c: Colour woodblock print, Mounter applying backing paper to folding screen by an unknown artist, Japan, 1785. Picture calendar print (egoyomi) for the year Tenmei 5 (1785). The character dai (large/long) and numbers for the long months 1, 3, 6, 7, 9, 10 and 12 are written on the mounter’s robe.

J_2315.o: Approved Category 2017/Printed Material/Print/Relief Print/Woodblock print; Object by Function/Documents by function/Egoyomi
J_2315.c: Colour woodblock print, Children running after manzai dancer by an unknown artist, printed in Japan, 1786. Egoyomi (picture calendar) print. Picture calendar print (egoyomi) for the year Tenmei 6 (1786). The character dai (large/long) and numbers for the long months are written on the robes of the taller dancer; the character shō (small/short) and numbers for the short months are written on the robes of the shorter dancer. Manzai dancers performed at New Year.

J_2316.o: Approved Category 2017/Printed Material/Print/Relief Print/Woodblock print; Object by Function/Documents by function/Egoyomi
J_2316.c: Colour woodblock print, Courtier on horseback by an unknown artist and printmaker Yoshida Gyosen, printed in Japan, 1786. Picture calendar print (egoyomi) for the year Tenmei 6 (1786), a Horse Year. The character dai (large/long) and numbers for the long months 2, 4, 7, 9, 10, intercalary 10 and 12 are written on the tree trunk. The aristocratic poet with one arm raised against falling cherry blossoms is probably a springtime reworking of the subject Fujiwara no Teika (1162-1241), who composed a poem about stopping his horse and covering his head with his sleeve as snow fell.

J_2317.t: Dancer with hand puppet of horse
J_2317.o: Approved Category 2017/Printed Material/Print/Relief Print/Woodblock print; Object by Function/Documents by function/Egoyomi
J_2317.c: Colour woodblock print, Dancer with hand puppet of horse by an unknown artist, printed in Japan, 1786. Picture calendar print (egoyomi) for the year Tenmei 6 (1786), a Horse Year. The character dai (large/long) and numbers for the long months 2, 4, 7, 9, 10, intercalary 10 and 12 are written on the dancer’s sleeves. The dancer is dressed for the harugoma, or spring pony dance.

J_2318.o: Approved Category 2017/Printed Material/Print/Relief Print/Woodblock print; Object by Function/Documents by function/Egoyomi
J_2318.c: Colour woodblock print, Maker of papier-mache dolls designed by an unknown artist and created by the printmaker Toen, printed in Japan, 1790. Picture calendar print (egoyomi) for the year Kansei 2 (1790), a Dog Year. The character dai (large/long) and numbers for the long months 1, 3, 4, 6, 9 and 11 are written on the sliding doors.

J_2319.o: Approved Category 2017/Printed Material/Print/Relief Print/Woodblock print; Object by Function/Documents by function/Egoyomi
J_2319.c: Colour woodblock print, Samurai beside a porch designed by an unknown artist and created by the printmaker Toen, printed in Japan, 1790. The samurai calls out to ask if anyone is home, with a play upon words switching the homophones 'isn't' and 'dog' ('inu'). Toen's name is associated with several picture calendar prints (egoyomi) in the Chester Beatty collection. Although this print lacks the calendar information expected of an egoyomi print, the pun indicates that it was made for a Dog Year.

J_2320.t: Couple retrieving shuttlecock from a plum tree
J_2320.o: Approved Category 2017/Printed Material/Print/Relief Print/Woodblock print; Object by Function/Documents by function/Egoyomi
J_2320.c: Colour woodblock print, Couple retrieving shuttlecock from a plum tree designed by an unknown artist and created by the printmaker Toen, printed in Japan, 1790. Picture calendar print (egoyomi) for the year Kansei 2 (1790). The numbers for the short months 2, 5, 7, 8, 10 and 12 are written on the woman’s sash.

J_2321.o: Approved Category 2017/Printed Material/Print/Relief Print/Woodblock print; Object by Function/Documents by function/Egoyomi
J_2321.c: Colour woodblock print, Old woman reading by an unknown artist, printed in Japan, possibly 1790. This print may have been intended to be a picture calendar (egoyomi) but the calendar information is missing, possibly trimmed away.

J_2322.t: Rats freeing Yukihime from the cherry tree
J_2322.o: Approved Category 2017/Printed Material/Print/Relief Print/Woodblock print; Object by Function/Documents by function/Egoyomi
J_2322.c: Colour woodblock print, Rats freeing Yukihime from the cherry tree designed by an unknown artist and created by the printmaker Toen, printed in Japan, 1792. Picture calendar print (egoyomi) for the year Kansei 4 (1792), a Rat Year. The numbers for the short months appear to be written on the Yukihime's sash. When the murderous Matsunaga Daizen ties Yukihime to a cherry tree and prepares to kill her husband in front of her, Yukihime draws rats in the dust at her feet. The rats spring to life and gnaw the ropes to free her.

J_2323.o: Approved Category 2017/Printed Material/Print/Relief Print/Woodblock print; Object by Function/Documents by function/Egoyomi
J_2323.c: Colour woodblock print, Mother, child and pet rat, designed by an unknown artist and created by the printmaker Toen, printed in Japan, 1792. Picture calendar print (egoyomi) for the year Kansei 4 (1792), a Rat Year. The character shō (small/short) and numbers for the short months 1, intercalary 2, 4, 7, 9 and 11 are written on the child’s robe.

J_2324.t: Street vendor pouring water over woman's hands
J_2324.o: Approved Category 2017/Printed Material/Print/Relief Print/Woodblock print; Object by Function/Documents by function/Egoyomi
J_2324.c: Colour woodblock print, Street vendor pouring water over woman's hands, designed by an unknown artist and created by the printmaker Toen, printed in Japan, 1796. Picture calendar print (egoyomi) for the year Kansei 8 (1796), a Dragon Year. The numbers for the short months are featured among the patterns on the vendor’s sash. Itinerant water sellers marketed their product as 'dragon water' (ryūsui), a homophone for 'running water', hence the decoration on the vendor's stand.

J_2325.t: Kiyohime and the bell of Dо̄jо̄ji
J_2325.o: Approved Category 2017/Printed Material/Print/Relief Print/Woodblock print; Object by Function/Documents by function/Egoyomi
J_2325.c: Colour woodblock print, Kiyohime and the bell of Dо̄jо̄ji designed by an unknown artist and created by the printmaker Toen, printed in Japan, 1796. Egoyomi (picture calendar) print. Picture calendar print (egoyomi) for the year Kansei 8 (1796), a Dragon Year. The numbers for the short months—1, 3, 5, 6, 8, 10—are featured on the roundels of Kiyohime’s robe. Kiyohime famously transformed into a serpent under the bell of Dōjōji when her love for a priest was unrequited: an appropriate subject for a Dragon Year. The placard beside Kiyohime should (according to the story) be inscribed 'kinsei' or 'forbidden', but instead playfully reads 'Kansei' - the name of the era in which the print was made.

J_2326.t: Tawara Tо̄da and Otohime on long bridge at Seta
J_2326.o: Approved Category 2017/Printed Material/Print/Relief Print/Woodblock print; Object by Function/Documents by function/Egoyomi
J_2326.c: Colour woodblock print, Tawara Tо̄da and Otohime on the long bridge at Seta designed by an unknown artist and created by the printmaker Toen, printed in Japan, 1796. Picture calendar print (egoyomi) for the year Kansei 8 (1796), a Dragon Year. The character shō (small/short) is printed on Otohime’s hair, and the numbers for the short months—1, 3, 5, 6, 8, 10—are featured on her robe. Otohime was the daughter of a dragon living in Lake Biwa who sought Tawara Tōda’s help against the giant centipede of Mt. Mikami.

J_2327.o: Approved Category 2017/Printed Material/Print/Relief Print/Woodblock print; Object by Function/Documents by function/Egoyomi
J_2327.c: Colour woodblock print, Woman sitting at writing desk designed by an unknown artist with printmaker mark Atago shita, printed in Japan, 1796. Picture calendar print (egoyomi) for the year Tenmei 8 (1796). The character dai (large/long) and numbers for the long months 2, 4, 7, 9, 11 and 12 are written on the book. The plaque over doorway above reads 'dragon year'.

J_2328.t: Lacquer box with two gold sword-hilt ornaments
J_2328.o: Approved Category 2017/Printed Material/Print/Relief Print/Woodblock print; Object by Function/Documents by function/Surimono
J_2328.c: Colour woodblock print, Lacquer box with two gold sword-hilt ornaments from the series 'Seven pictures for Shо̄fudai' (Shо̄fudai shichiban no uchi) by an unknown artist, Japan, 1810s. Surimono print made for the Shо̄fu group with poem signed Suichо̄dai Yanamori of Kanaya. Shо̄fudai was the leader of the Shо̄fu poetry group. The sword-hilt ornaments (menuki) are in the form of peony flowers, as referenced in the poem.

J_2329.t: Asaina throwing beans at a demon
J_2329.o: Approved Category 2017/Printed Material/Print/Relief Print/Woodblock print; Object by Function/Documents by function/Surimono
J_2329.c: Colour woodblock print, Asaina throwing beans at a demon by an unknown artist, printed in Japan, 1810s. Surimono print. During the festival of Setsubun, beans are thrown to purify the home and cast out demons. Here, legendary hero Asaina takes his turn to cast out out a cowering demon. The signature of Hokusai (printed on the right hand side) uses a different colour ink to the keyblock and is understood to be a later, spurious, addition.

J_2330.o: Approved Category 2017/Printed Material/Print/Relief Print/Woodblock print; Object by Function/Documents by function/Surimono
J_2330.c: Colour woodblock print, Sarugenji and Keika from an untitled series of illustrations for Sarugenji designed by an unknown artist, printed in Japan, possibly 1824. Surimono print with poems signed Shin'о̄tei Shikori, Banritei Hiromaru, Shinsо̄tei Yamamatsu, Bankitei Kо̄ra and Shinratei Manzо̄. In the story of Sarugenji (monkey Genji), Sarugenji is a sardine seller who abandoned his wife to travel to the capital. There he falls in love with Keika, a prostitute. They share a passion for poetry and literature.

J_2331.o: Approved Category 2017/Printed Material/Print/Relief Print/Woodblock print; Object by Function/Documents by function/Surimono
J_2331.c: Colour woodblock print, Sarugenji meets Keika from an untitled series of illustrations for Sarugenji designed by an unknown artist, printed in Japan, possibly 1824. Surimono print with poems signed Shirakawa Yobune and Shinratei Manzо̄. In the story of Sarugenji (monkey Genji), Sarugenji is a sardine seller who abandoned his wife to travel to the capital. There he falls in love with Keika, a prostitute. They share a passion for poetry and literature.

J_2332.o: Approved Category 2017/Printed Material/Print/Relief Print/Woodblock print; Object by Function/Documents by function/Surimono
J_2332.c: Colour woodblock print, Courtier presenting bamboo to lady by an unknown artist, Japan, mid-1820s. Shikishiban format, surimono print with poems signed Gochikutei Manao and Kyōkadō Magao.

J_2333.t: Crowd outside gate of Chinese city
J_2333.o: Approved Category 2017/Printed Material/Print/Relief Print/Woodblock print; Object by Function/Documents by function/Surimono
J_2333.c: Colour woodblock print, Crowd outside gate of Chinese city by an unknown artist, Japan, possibly 1825. Shikishiban format, surimono print with poems signed Tetsunoya Ōmon, Enritsuen Chiei and Yomo Utagaki Magao.

J_2334.t: Woman and child in Yoshiwara brothel
J_2334.o: Approved Category 2017/Printed Material/Print/Relief Print/Woodblock print; Object by Function/Documents by function/Surimono
J_2334.c: Colour woodblock print, Woman and child in Yoshiwara brothel by an unknown artist, Japan, early or mid-1830s. Shikishiban format, surimono print with poems signed Rikkaen Fusanaga and Shakuyakutei.

J_2335.t: Prince Genji first catches sight of Murasaki
J_2335.o: Approved Category 2017/Printed Material/Print/Relief Print/Woodblock print; Object by Function/Documents by function/Surimono
J_2335.c: Colour woodblock print, Prince Genji first catches sight of Murasaki, by an unknown artist, Japan, 1837. Shikishiban format, surimono print with poems signed Kajuan and Shūchōdō.

J_2336.c: Colour woodblock print, Fish in net by Kisui, Japan, 1875-1900. Shijō school colour print.

J_2337.o: Approved Category 2017/Printed Material/Print/Relief Print/Woodblock print; Object by Function/Documents by function/Surimono
J_2337.c: Colour woodblock print, Leaf by Ueda Kōchō, Japan, 1820s. Shijō school surimono print. The poems have been trimmed from the print.

J_2338.t: Tray with scissors and leaves in porcelain bowl
J_2338.o: Approved Category 2017/Printed Material/Print/Relief Print/Woodblock print; Object by Function/Documents by function/Surimono
J_2338.c: Colour woodblock print, Tray with scissors and leaves in porcelain bowl by Shibata Zeshin, Japan, possibly 1855. Shikishiban format, Shijō school surimono print.

J_2339.o: Approved Category 2017/Printed Material/Print/Relief Print/Woodblock print; Object by Function/Documents by function/Surimono
J_2339.c: Colour woodblock print, Dandelions by Shibata Zeshin, Japan, 1850-1875. Probably a section from a larger Shijō school surimono print.

J_2340.t: Final act of Treasury of loyal retainers (Chūshingura ōgiri)
J_2340.c: Colour woodblock print, ‘Final act of Treasury of loyal retainers’ (Chūshingura ōgiri) from the series ‘Parlour puppets’ (Ozashiki ningyō) by Utagawa Toyohiro, Japan, c. 1801-1804. Nishiki-e print.

J_2341.c: Colour woodblock print, Standing screen of tiger by Kawanabe Kyōsai, Japan, 1878.

J_2342.c: Colour woodblock print, Flower arrangements by Katsukawa Shunsen, Japan, early 19th century.

a: Hishikawa Moronobu, attributed to; Urokogataya Sanzaemon, attributed to
J_2401.c: Woodblock print of Kunitaka's daughter kidnapped by demons from an untitled series of prints of the story of Shutendōji attributed to Hishikawa Moronobu and published by Urokogataya Sanzaemon in Edo (modern Tokyo), Japan, around 1680. Yoko-ōban format, sumizuri-e print.

J_2402.t: Fish for sale (Sakana uri de gozaimasu)
a: Torii Kiyomasu; Komatsuya Denshichirō, probably by
J_2402.c: Woodblock print, 'Fish for sale' (Sakana uri de gozaimasu) by Torii Kiyomasu, published by Komatsuya (possibly Komatsuya Denshichirō) in Edo (modern Tokyo), Japan, around 1714. Yoko-ōban format, sumizuri-e print. The cross-shaped crests worn by the fish seller identify him as actor Ōtani Hiroji I. Making his debut in 1700, Hiroji enjoyed considerable success on stage and was known for playing leading roles. A near identical depiction of Hiroji as a fish seller (though without octopus) is featured as a toy doll in a print by Okumura Masanobu.

J_2403.t: Murasaki Shikibu at Ishiyama Temple (Ishiyama-dera no Murasaki Shikibu)
a: Torii Kiyomasu; Komatsuya Denshichirō, probably by
J_2403.c: Woodblock print, 'Murasaki shikibu at Ishiyama Temple' (Ishiyama-dera no Murasaki Shikibu) by Torii Kiyomasu, published by Komatsuya (possibly Komatsuya Denshichirō) in Edo (modern Tokyo), Japan, between 1711 and 1716. Yoko-ōban format, sumizuri-e print.

J_2404.t: Allusion to Grasses of Musashi Plain (Musashino) from Tales of Ise (Ise monogatari)
J_2404.c: Colour woodblock print, Allusion to 'Grasses of Musashi Plain' (Musashino) from 'Tales of Ise' (Ise monogatari) by Torii Kiyohiro, published by Maruya Kuzaemon in Edo (modern Tokyo), Japan, between 1751 and 1764. Ōban format, benizuri-e print. In a field of autumn grasses, an elegant young man carries a woman on his shoulders. The scene is a representation (mitate) of the famous runaway lovers in the Grasses of Musashi Plain, Chapter 12 of the Tales of Ise.

J_2405.c: Colour woodblock print of a party in the Yoshiwara, from the series 'Twelve bouts of lovemaking' (Shikidō tokkumi jūni-tsugai) by Isoda Koryūsai, printed in Japan around 1777. Ōban format, nishiki-e print. This is the first sheet in a set of twelve erotic prints comparing sexual positions to wrestling holds. As is often the case with suites of explicitly erotic ukiyo-e prints (known as shunga or 'spring pictures' in Japanese), the frontispiece is relatively coy when compared to the works that follow.

J_2406.t: Making her debut in the eighth month: Senzan of the Chōjiya house (Hachigatsu tsukidashi Chōjiya no Senzan)
J_2406.c: Colour woodblock print, 'Making her debut in the eighth month: Senzan of the Chōjiya house' (Hachigatsu tsukidashi Chōjiya no Senzan) from the series 'Models for fashion: New year designs fresh as young leaves' (Hinagata wakana no hatsu moyō) by Isoda Koryūsai, published by Nishimuraya Yohachi in Edo (modern Tokyo), Japan, around 1778. Ōban format, nishiki-e print. Featuring only Koryūsai's signature and the publishers mark, this print lacks the title cartouche and text found on other examples of this design that identify Senzan of the Chōjiya house.

J_2407.c: Colour woodblock print, 'Kayoiji of the Echizenya house' from the series 'Models for fashion: New year designs fresh as young leaves' (Hinagata wakana no hatsu moyō) by Isoda Koryūsai, published by Nishimuraya Yohachi in Edo (modern Tokyo), Japan, around 1778 to 1780. Ōban format, nishiki-e print. A lengthy handwritten inscription in English describes the dress and complexion of Japanese women, using the print for reference. Mention is also made of the 'maids' that attend them. In the original Japanese text, Kayoiji's attendants are identified as Wakaba and Wakaki.

J_2408.c: Colour woodblock print, 'Kinshū of the Yotsumeya house' from the series 'Models for fashion: New year designs fresh as young leaves' (Hinagata wakana no hatsu moyō) by Isoda Koryūsai, published by Nishimuraya Yohachi in Edo (modern Tokyo), Japan, around 1777. Ōban format, nishiki-e print.

J_2409.c: Colour woodblock print, 'Takigawa of the Tamaya house' from the series 'Models for fashion: New year designs fresh as young leaves' (Hinagata wakana no hatsu moyō) by Isoda Koryūsai, published by Nishimuraya Yohachi in Edo (modern Tokyo), Japan, around 1778 to 1780. Ōban format, nishiki-e print.

J_2410.c: Colour woodblock print, Umenoka of the Kado-Tamaya house from the series 'Models for fashion: New year designs fresh as young leaves' (Hinagata wakana no hatsu moyō) by Isoda Koryūsai, published by Nishimuraya Yohachi in Edo (modern Tokyo), Japan, around 1778. Ōban format, nishiki-e print.

J_2411.c: Woodblock print of a Yoshiwara scene by Okumura Masanobu, printed in Japan around 1710. Sumizuri-e print.

J_2412.t: Naka-no-chō in the Yoshiwara (Yoshiwara naka no chō)
J_2412.c: Woodblock print, 'Naka-no-chō in the Yoshiwara' (Yoshiwara naka no chō) by Okumura Masanobu, printed in Japan in the 1710s. Yoko-ōban format, sumizuri-e print. This print is number four in an untitled series depicting a visit to the Yoshiwara, known as 'Series L'. Masanobu's signature is included on the final print in the series.

J_2413.t: Print from Mirror of new Yoshiwara courtesans with samples of their calligraphy (Yoshiwara keisei shin bijin awase jihitsu kagami)
J_2413.c: Colour woodblock print from the album 'Mirror of new Yoshiwara courtesans with samples of their calligraphy' (Yoshiwara keisei shin bijin awase jihitsu kagami) by Kitao Masanobu, published by Tsutaya Jūzaburō in Edo (modern Tokyo), Japan, in 1784. Page from an album, nishiki-e print.

J_2414.t: Plum tree where the warbler dwells (Ōshukubai) from Willow strands (Yanagi no ito)
J_2414.c: Colour woodblock print, 'Plum tree where the warbler dwells' (Ōshukubai) by Kitao Shigemasa from the book 'Willow strands' (Yanagi no ito) published by Tsutaya Jūzaburō in Edo (modern Tokyo), Japan, in 1797. Page from a poetry anthology, nishiki-e print.

a: Kitao Shigemasa, attributed to; Nishimuraya Yohachi
J_2415.c: Colour woodblock print of ‘Seven lucky gods’ attributed to Kitao Shigemasa, published by Nishimuraya Yohachi; printed in Edo (modern Tokyo), Japan, during the 1770s. Pictured together on their treasure ship, Japan’s Seven Gods of Good Fortune are an auspicious company drawn from diverse traditions. The musical goddess Benzaiten, hammer-carrying Daikokuten, round-bellied Hotei and fierce guardian king Bishamonten all came to Japan through Buddhism. Invoked for long life, Fukurokuju and Jurōjin have their origins in Chinese Daoism. Ebisu is identified with deities of Japan’s indigenous Shintō faith; often shown fishing, here he is depicted with a red snapper.

J_2416.t: Perspective view of sleeping dragon plum tree in the plum garden at Kameido (Uki-e Kameido umeyashiki garyōbai no zu)
J_2416.c: Colour woodblock print, 'Perspective view of sleeping dragon plum tree in the plum garden at Kameido' (Uki-e Kameido umeyashiki garyōbai no zu) by Kitao Shigemasa, published by Nishimuraya Yohachi in Edo (modern Tokyo), Japan, between 1775 and 1785. Yoko-ōban format, nishiki-e print. People gather at the Kameido plum garden to enjoy the first blossoms upon the garden’s renowned ‘sleeping dragon’ plum tree, a welcome signal of winter’s end.

J_2417.t: Perspective view of people enjoying cool evening at the river bed at Shijō, Kyoto (Uki-e Kyōtō Shijō kawahara yūsuzumi zu)
J_2417.c: Colour woodblock print, 'Perspective view of people enjoying cool evening at the river bed at Shijō, Kyoto' (Uki-e Kyōto Shijō kawahara yūsuzumi zu) by Utagawa Toyoharu, published by Nishimuraya Yohachi in Edo (modern Tokyo), Japan, between 1772 and 1781. Yoko-ōban format, nishiki-e print.

J_2418.c: Colour woodblock print, Winding stream party by Kubo Shunman printed in Japan, around 1815. Left sheet from a triptych, ōban format, nishiki-e print.

J_2419.c: Colour woodblock print, Cherry blossom viewing at Ueno by Angyūsai Enshi, published by an unidentified publisher (called 'Maru-matsu' after their mark) in Edo (modern Tokyo), Japan, between 1781 and 1789. Thought to be one sheet from a triptych, ōban format, nishiki-e print.

J_2420.c: Colour woodblock print, Trying on kimono from the series 'Patterns for modern beauties' (Tōsei bijin onna hinagata) by Torii Kiyomine published by in Nishimuraya Yohachi in Edo (modern Tokyo), Japan, between 1804 and 1811. Ōban format, nishiki-e print.

J_2421.c: Woodblock print of the 'Eleventh month' (Jūichi gatsu) from the series 'Twelve months of the southern quarter' (Minami jūni ko) by Torii Kiyonaga, printed in ink and colours on paper in Japan, c. 1783.

J_2422.t: Returning from the bathhouse in rain
J_2422.c: Colour woodblock print, Returning from the bathhouse in rain from the series 'Current manners in eastern brocade' (Fūzoku azuma no nishiki) by Torii Kiyonaga, printed in Japan around 1774. Ōban format, nishiki-e print.

J_2423.t: Actors Ichikawa Danjurō V, Nakamura Rikō I and Sawamura Sōjūrō III
J_2423.c: Colour woodblock print of actors Ichikawa Danjurō V, Nakamura Rikō I and Sawamura Sōjūrō III by Torii Kiyonaga, published by Kōzuya Isuke in Edo (modern Tokyo), Japan, in 1784. Ōban format, nishiki-e print. Dated to 1784, this print is based upon the special season-opening ('kaomise') performance of the play 'Big business on leech island' (Ōakinai hiru ga kojima) at the Nakamura-za theatre in Edo. Actor Ichikawa Danjurō V performs as Matano Gorō Kagehisa and Sawamura Sōjūrō III plays Kawazu Saburō Sukeyasu. Engaged in a game of go, they are presided over by Nakamura Rikō I as the shirabyōshi dancer Kazaori, daughter of Kamata Masakiyo.

J_2424.t: Shop of Nishimuraya Yohachi from Colours of the triple dawn (Saishiki mitsu no asa)
J_2424.c: Colour woodblock print of the shop of Nishimuraya Yohachi from 'Colours of the triple dawn' (Saishiki mitsu no asa) by Torii Kiyonaga, published by Nishimuraya Yohachi in Edo (modern Tokyo) in 1787. Ōban format page from an illustrated album, nishiki-e print. The first day of the first month of a new year becomes a triple dawn, captured here in full colour. Originally prepared as the last image in an elegant album of seven new years' scenes, this print has no central crease and so may not have been part of a bound volume. It shows the shop of publisher Nishimuraya Yohachi, also known by the company name Eijudō. Nishimuraya's shop bustles with customers, eagerly buying his freshly-published prints.

J_2425.c: Colour woodblock print, Young girl and attendants from the series 'Current manners in eastern brocade' (Fūzoku azuma no nishiki) by Torii Kiyonaga, printed in Japan around 1774. Ōban format, nishiki-e print.

J_2426.t: Actors Sawamura Sōjūrō III, Nakayama Kojūrō VI, Ōtani Hiroji III and Ichikawa Yaozō III
J_2426.c: Preparatory drawing for woodblock print of actors Sawamura Sōjūrō III, Nakayama Kojūrō VI, Ōtani Hiroji III and Ichikawa Yaozō III by Torii Kiyonaga, drawn in ink on paper in Japan in 1785. Preparatory drawing (shita-e) for ōban format print. Dated to 1785, this image is drawn from the special season-opening ('kaomise') performance of 'Yukimotsutake furisode Genji' at the Nakamura Theatre in Edo. The print shows Sawamura Sōjūrō III performing as Taira no Shigemori, Nakayama Kojūrō VI as Kiheiji, Ōtani Hiroji III as Miura Arajiro, and Ichikawa Yaozō III as Akugenta Yoshihira. Examples of the finished print can be found in the collections of Minneapolis Institute of Art (no. 74.1.128) and the Art Institute of Chicago (no. 1934.254).

J_2427.t: Boys' festival in the fifth month
J_2427.c: Colour woodblock print, Boys' festival in the fifth month from the series 'Games of precious children for five festivals' (Kodakara gosetsu asobi) by Torii Kiyonaga, published by Tsutaya Jūzaburō Edo (modern Tokyo), Japan, in 1801. Ōban format, nishiki-e print.

J_2428.c: Colour woodblock print, Women under cherry blossoms from the series 'Contest of contemporary beauties of the pleasure quarters' (Tōsei yūri bijin awase) by Torii Kiyonaga, printed in Japan around 1774. Right sheet from a diptych, ōban format, nishiki-e print.

J_2429.t: Actors Mimasu Tokujirō I and Matsumoto Kōshirō IV in scene from 'Koi no hikyaku'
J_2429.c: Colour woodblock print of actors Mimasu Tokujirō I and Matsumoto Kōshirō IV in scene from 'Koi no hikyaku' by Torii Kiyonaga, printed in Japan in 1784. Ōban format, nishiki-e print. The play 'Koi no hikyaku' was peformed at the Morita-za theatre, Edo, in 1784. Here, Matsumoto Kōshirō plays Chūbei and Mimasu Tokujirō performs as Umegawa before chanters Tomimoto Itsukidayū and Tomimoto Hisatayū, and accompanist Namizaki Tokuji.

J_2430.t: Child prodigy Gyokkashi Shima Eimo giving a reading lesson (Gyokkashi Shima Eimo sodoku no tai)
J_2430.c: Colour woodblock print, 'Child prodigy Gyokkashi Shima Eimo giving a reading lesson' (Gyokkashi Shima Eimo sodoku no tai) by Torii Kiyonaga, published by Nishimuraya Yohachi in Edo (modern Tokyo), Japan, around 1785. Ōban format, nishiki-e print.

J_2431.t: Actor Ichikawa Danjūrō II as Sanada no Yoichi
J_2431.c: Woodblock print with hand-applied colour of actor Ichikawa Danjūrō II as Sanada no Yoichi by Torii Kiyomasu II, published by Murataya Jirōbei in Edo (modern Tokyo), Japan, in 1725. Hosoban format, urushi-e print. The print shows Ichikawa Danjūrō II's dramatic arrival on stage as Sanada no Yoichi in the play 'Diary kept on a voyage to Izu' (Funadama Izu nikki) performed in Edo's Nakamura-za theatre in 1725. This kind of hand-coloured woodblock print is known as an urushi-e or 'lacquer picture', so named for the glossy black finish achieved by applying animal glue to areas of black ink.

J_2432.c: Woodblock print with hand-applied colour, Youth dancing attributed to Torii Kiyomasu II, printed in Japan, around 1720. Hosoban format, urushi-e print. The subject of this print appears to be a male youth or 'wakashu', though the indicative shaved part of his hairstyle is not clearly shown. Hand-coloured prints of this type with particularly glossy black ink are known as an urushi-e or 'lacquer pictures'. The gloss finish is achieved by applying animal glue to the inked areas.

J_2433.c: Woodblock print with hand-applied colour, Woman in black raincoat by Okumura Masanobu, printed in Japan, around 1738. Hosoban format, urushi-e print in fan shape. This kind of hand-coloured woodblock print is known as an urushi-e or 'lacquer picture'. Named for the glossy black finish achieved by applying animal glue to areas of black ink, here the technique is used to emphasise the soaked raincoat.

J_2434.c: Woodblock print with hand-applied colour of actor Uemura Kichisaburō attributed to Okumura Masanobu, printed in Japan, c. 1740. Hosoban format, possibly part of a multiple-sheet work.

J_2435.c: Woodblock print with hand-applied colour, Attendant handing letter to courtesan designed and published by Okumura Masanobu in Edo (modern Tokyo), Japan, between 1716 and 1736. Hosoban format, urushi-e print.

J_2436.t: Actors Ichikawa Monnosuke I as Fukakusa no shōshō and Arashi Wakano I as Ono no Komachi
J_2436.c: Woodblock print with hand-applied colour of actors Ichikawa Monnosuke I as Fukakusa no shōshō and Arashi Wakano I as Ono no Komachi by Okumura Toshinobu, published by Sōshūya in Japan, probably between 1723 and 1725. Hosoban format, urushi-e print. This kind of hand-coloured woodblock print is known as an urushi-e or 'lacquer picture', so named for the glossy black finish achieved by applying animal glue to areas of black ink.

J_2437.t: Young women's fashion: Flower patterned furisode (Hana no furisode musumefū)
J_2437.c: Woodblock print with hand-applied colour, 'Young women's fashion: Flower patterned furisode' (Hana no furisode musumefū) by Okumura Toshinobu, published by Komatsuya in Edo (modern Tokyo), Japan, between 1716 and 1736. Hosoban format, urushi-e print.

J_2438.t: Princess Shikishi and Nowake visit Fujiwara Teika at Ogura
J_2438.c: Woodblock print with hand-applied colour, Princess Shikishi and Nowake visit Fujiwara Teika at Ogura by Nishimura Shigenaga, published by Igaya Kan'emon in Edo (modern Tokyo), Japan, between 1716 and 1736. Hosoban format, urushi-e print. This kind of hand-coloured woodblock print is known as an urushi-e or 'lacquer picture', so named for the glossy black finish achieved by applying animal glue to areas of black ink.

J_2439.t: Woman admiring Sanogawa Ichimatsu I from Triptych of hanging scrolls: Playing with reality (Kakemono sanpuku-tsui utsutsu no asobi)
J_2439.c: Woodblock print, Woman admiring Sanogawa Ichimatsu I from 'Triptych of hanging scrolls: Playing with reality' (Kakemono sanpuku-tsui utsutsu no asobi) by Nishimura Shigenaga, published by Shusseidō in Edo (modern Tokyo), Japan, c. 1750. Hosoban format, key-block print. First established as an actor in Kyoto, Sanogawa Ichimatsu I went to Edo in 1741. Chequerboard motifs became popular after he wore them on stage. Known as the 'Ichimatsu pattern', they were closely associated with the actor and here adorn the admiring prostitute's obi (sash) . Uncut impressions of the complete hosoban triptych, printed with colour, can be found in the collections of the Royal Ontario Museum and MFA Boston. While the printed title identifies the Chester Beatty print as the right sheet of the set, this refers to the proper right. For the viewer, this would be the left sheet of the composition.

J_2440.c: Woodblock print with hand-applied colour, Young man holding fan by Nishimura Shigenaga, printed in Japan, around 1745. Hosoban format, urushi-e print. This print is very similar to a print in the collections of MFA Boston, which carries in addition a publisher's mark (Igaya) and title cartouche ('In the style of a young man: Left sheet of a triptych'). The patterns of the youth's clothing are the same in both prints, but the black ink is differently applied. The relationship between these works is yet to be determined.

J_2441.c: Woodblock print with hand-applied colour, Pedlar from Ōhara by Nishimura Shigenaga, published by Tsuruya Kiemon in Edo (modern Tokyo), Japan, between 1716 and 1736. Hosoban format, urushi-e print. The 'Ōharame' or women from the rustic village of Ōhara, Kyoto, were pedlars of firewood praised for their beauty.

J_2442.t: Actors Bandō Hikosaburō II as Sanada Yoichi and Arashi Hinaji as Maiko Uryūno
J_2442.c: Colour woodblock print of actors Bandō Hikosaburō II as Sanada Yoichi and Arashi Hinaji as Maiko Uryūno by Torii Kiyomitsu, published by Urokogataya Magobei in Edo (modern Tokyo), Japan, in 1763. Hosoban format, benizuri-e print.

J_2443.t: Actors Ichimura Kamezō as Kyō no Jirō and Segawa Kikunojō II as Midaregami no Osen
J_2443.c: Colour woodblock print of actors Ichimura Kamezō as Kyō no Jirō and Segawa Kikunojō II as Midaregami no Osen by Torii Kiyomitsu, published by Maruya Kohei in Edo (modern Tokyo), Japan, in 1761. Hosoban format, benizuri-e print. The scene is taken from the play 'Edo murasaki kongen soga' performed at the Ichimura-za theatre in 1761. Ichimura Kamezō plays the ferryman Kyō no Jirō, and Segawa Kikunojō II plays Midaregami no Osen, shown here at the bank of the Sumida river.

J_2444.t: Actor Ōtani Hiroji III as Yazama Jūtarō
J_2444.c: Colour woodblock print of actor Ōtani Hiroji III as Yazama Jūtarō by Torii Kiyomitsu, published by Harimaya Shinshichi in Edo (modern Tokyo), Japan, in 1767. Hosoban format, benizuri-e print.

J_2445.c: Colour woodblock print, 'Kikusui section of Taiheiki' by Torii Kiyomitsu, published by Maruya Kohei in Edo (modern Tokyo), Japan, around 1759. Hosoban format, benizuri-e print.

J_2446.t: Actor Onoe Kikugorō I as Yoshimine no shōshō Koresada
J_2446.c: Colour woodblock print of actor Onoe Kikugorō I as Yoshimine no shōshō Koresada by Torii Kiyomitsu, published by Tomitaya in Edo (modern Tokyo), Japan, in 1762. Hosoban format, benizuri-e print.

J_2447.t: Actor Ichimura Kamezō I as Higashiyama Yorikane
J_2447.c: Colour woodblock print of actor Ichimura Kamezō I as Higashiyama Yorikane by Torii Kiyomitsu, published by Maruya Kuzaemon in Edo (modern Tokyo), Japan, in 1759. Hosoban format, benizuri-e print.

J_2448.t: Hawk from Triptych of lucky first dreams of the new year (Hatsuyume sanpuku-tsui)
J_2448.c: Colour woodblock print, Hawk from 'Triptych of lucky first dreams of the new year' (Hatsuyume sanpuku-tsui) by Ishikawa Toyonobu, published by Emiya Kichiemon in Edo (modern Tokyo), Japan, between 1744 and 1755. Hosoban format, benizuri-e print.

J_2449.c: Colour woodblock print, Daruma receives a massage by Ishikawa Toyonobu, published by Urokogataya Magobei in Edo (modern Tokyo), Japan, between 1751 and 1764. Hosoban format, benizuri-e print.

J_2450.c: Colour woodblock print of actor Nakamura Kiyosaburō I by Ishikawa Toyonobu, published by Urokogataya Magobei in Edo (modern Tokyo), Japan, between 1751 and 1757. Hosoban format, benizuri-e print.

J_2451_1.c: Colour woodblock print, 'Third month' (Sangatsu) from the series 'Customs of the twelve months' (Tsukinami fūzoku) by Ishikawa Toyonobu, printed in Japan between 1751 and 1756. Tanzakuban format, benizuri-e print.

J_2451_2.c: Colour woodblock print, 'Fourth month' (Shigatsu) from the series 'Customs of the twelve months' (Tsukinami fūzoku) by Ishikawa Toyonobu, printed in Japan between 1751 and 1756. Tanzakuban format, benizuri-e print.

J_2452.t: Actors Segawa Kichiji II and Bandō Hikosaburō II
J_2452.c: Colour woodblock print of actors Segawa Kichiji II and Bandō Hikosaburō II by Torii Kiyohiro, published by Maruya Kuzaemon in Edo (modern Tokyo), Japan, in 1756. Hosoban format, benizuri-e print. The print shows Segawa Kichiji II performing as Matsuwaka and Bandō Hikosaburō II as Mumewaka in the play 'Ume Wakana Futaba Soga', staged at the Ichimura-za theatre in 1756.

J_2453.t: Actor Onoe Kikugorō I as Usami Saburō disguised as Sano Jirōzaemon
J_2453.c: Colour woodblock print of actor Onoe Kikugorō I as Usami Saburō disguised as Sano Jirōzaemon by Torii Kiyohiro, published by Sakaiya Kurobei in Edo (modern Tokyo), Japan, in 1756. Hosoban format, benizuri-e print.

J_2454.t: Youth holding branch of cherry blossoms
J_2454.c: Colour woodblock print, 'Youth holding branch of cherry blossoms' by Torii Kiyohiro, published by Maruya Kohei in Edo (modern Tokyo), Japan, between 1751 and 1757. Hosoban format, benizuri-e print. A fashionable youth passes the torii gate of a shrine clutching a branch of cherry blossom; a short poem describes the blossoms that fall onto his robe.

J_2455.t: Actor Ichikawa Danjurō IV as Matsuōmaru
J_2455.c: Colour woodblock print of actor Ichikawa Danjurō IV as Matsuōmaru by Torii Kiyotsune, published by Nishinomiya Shinroku in Edo (modern Tokyo), Japan, in 1764. Hosoban format, benizuri-e print. In this print, Ichikawa Danjurō IV is shown performing in the play 'Sugawara and the secrets of calligraphy' (Sugawara denju tenarai kagami), staged at Edo's Nakamura-za theatre in 1764. He plays Matsuōmaru, depicted here in the struggle for the carriage scene.

J_2456.t: Actor Yamashita Kinsaku II as tea-seller Omiya
J_2456.c: Colour woodblock print of actor Yamashita Kinsaku II as tea-seller Omiya by Torii Kiyotsune, published by Yamanouchi in Edo (modern Tokyo), Japan, between 1772 and 1781. Hosoban format, nishiki-e print.

J_2457.t: Actor Arashi Sangorō II as Tomoenojō
J_2457.c: Colour woodblock print of actor Arashi Sangorō II as Tomoenojō by Torii Kiyotsune, published by Maruya Kuzaemon in Edo (modern Tokyo), Japan, in 1773. Hosoban format, nishiki-e print.

J_2458.t: Actor Ichimura Kamezō I as Soga no Gorō Tokimune
J_2458.c: Colour woodblock print of actor Ichimura Kamezō I as Soga no Gorō Tokimune by Yamamoto Fujinobu, published by Maruya Kuzaemon in Edo (modern Tokyo), Japan, in 1758. Hosoban format, benizuri-e print. The print shows a scene from the play 'Kujūsan-ki ōyose Soga', staged at Edo's Ichimura-za theatre in 1758.

J_2459.c: Colour woodblock print, 'New year's dream' from the series 'Prosperous flowers of the elegant twelve months' (Fūryū jūniki no eiga) by Isoda Koryūsai, printed in Japan around 1773. Trimmed nishiki-e print. A young couple are pictured at New Year. As they doze, they share a dream of Mt Fuji, a hawk and a crop of aubergines: a lucky combination for the first dream of the New Year. This is the first sheet in a set of twelve prints exploring sexual encounters across the twelve months. As is often the case with suites of explicitly erotic ukiyo-e prints (known as shunga or 'spring pictures' in Japanese), the first image is relatively coy when compared to the works that follow.

J_2460.t: Actors Yamashita Matatarō I as Takebe Genzō and Nakamura Tomijūrō I as Kiyo
J_2460.c: Colour woodblock print of actors Yamashita Matatarō I as Takebe Genzō and Nakamura Tomijūrō I as Kiyo by Yamamoto Yoshinobu, published by Maruya Kuzaemon in Edo (modern Tokyo), Japan, in 1756. Hosoban format, benizuri-e print. The print shows the 'Village school' scene from the play 'Sugawara and the secrets of calligraphy' (Sugawara denju tenarai kagami), staged at the Nakamura Theatre in 1756. Yamashita Matatarō I performs as Takebe Genzō and Nakamura Tomijūrō I plays Kiyo (or Chiyo), the wife of Matsuōmaru.

J_2461.c: Colour woodblock print, 'Matsukaze of the Ōgiya house' by Komai Yoshinobu, published by Maruya Kohei in Edo (modern Tokyo), Japan, in 1770. Chūban format, nishiki-e print. The title cartouche is in the shape of a folded letter similar to that passed to Matsukaze by her attendant. Above, the address of the Ōgiya brothel is given as block one of the Yoshiwara's Edo-cho. The names of other women at the Ōgiya are given together with those of their attendants. Cross referencing these names with contemporary guides to the Yoshiwara, the print can be dated to 1770.

J_2462.t: One sheet from Diptych of seven lucky gods (Shichifukujin ni-mai tsudzuki)
J_2462.c: Colour woodblock print, one sheet from 'Diptych of seven lucky gods' (Shichifukujin ni-mai tsudzuki) from the series 'Niwaka Festival Skits in the Yoshiwara' (Seirō Niwaka kyōgen) by Isoda Koryūsai, published by Nishimuraya Yohachi in Edo (modern Tokyo), Japan, around 1784. Chūban format, nishiki-e print. The Niwaka Festival was held in the Yoshiwara from the middle of the 8th month until the middle of the 9th month. In this print (one half of a diptych), denizens of Edo-chō's 2-chōme perform as four of the Seven Lucky Gods: Ebisu, Bishamonten, Hotei and Daikokuten.

J_2463.c: Colour woodblock print, Shrine maidens dancing by Ippitsusai Bunchō, printed in Japan in 1769. Hosoban format, nishiki-e print.

J_2464.t: Actors Bandō Mitsugorō I as Hanbei and Yamashita Kinsaku as Ochiyo
J_2464.c: Colour woodblock print of actors Bandō Mitsugorō I as Hanbei and Yamashita Kinsaku as Ochiyo by Ippitsusai Bunchō, printed in Japan in 1770. Hosoban format, nishiki-e print.

J_2465.c: Colour woodblock print, Poem by Jakuren Hōshi from the series 'Fashionable sleeves for three evening poems' (Fūryū tagasode sanseki) by Isoda Koryūsai, printed in Japan between 1772 and 1776. Chūban format, nishiki-e print.

J_2466.c: Colour woodblock print, Preparing to go out from the series 'Humorous poems of the willow' (Haifū yanagidaru) by Torii Kiyonaga, printed in Japan around 1785. Chūban format, nishiki-e print.

J_2467.c: Colour woodblock print, Three flute players by Torii Kiyonaga, published by Nishimuraya Yohachi in Edo (modern Tokyo), Japan, around 1781. Chūban format, nishiki-e print.

J_2468.c: Colour woodblock print, 'Sumida river' (Sumida gawa) from the series 'Collection of famous places in Edo' (Edo meisho shū) by Torii Kiyonaga, printed in Japan around 1782. Chūban format, nishiki-e print.

J_2469.c: Colour woodblock print, 'Playing with sparklers' from the series 'Mirror of women's customs' (Onna fūzoku masu kagami) by Torii Kiyonaga, printed in Japan around 1790. Chūban format, nishiki-e print.

J_2470.c: Colour woodblock print, Reading a Yoshiwara guidebook from the series 'Humorous poems of the willow' (Haifū yanagidaru) by Torii Kiyonaga, published by Tsuruya Kiemon in Edo (modern Tokyo), Japan, around 1790. Chūban format, nishiki-e print.

J_2471.c: Colour woodblock print, Women watching salt burning by Suzuki Harunobu, printed in Japan between 1765 and 1770. Chūban format, nishiki-e print.

J_2472.c: Colour woodblock print, Oiran (prostitute) parading with attendants by Suzuki Harunobu, printed in Japan around 1766. Chūban format, nishiki-e print.

J_2473.c: Colour woodblock print, 'Ofude of the Hayashiya teahouse' by Suzuki Harunobu, printed in Japan between 1765 and 1770. Chūban format, nishiki-e print.

J_2474.c: Colour woodblock print, Children with cat and mouse by Suzuki Harunobu, printed in Japan around 1768. Chūban format, nishiki-e print.

J_2475.c: Colour woodblock print, 'Chōfu jewel river' (Chōfu no tamagawa) from an untitled series of 'Six jewel rivers' by Suzuki Harunobu, printed in Japan around 1768. Chūban format, nishiki-e print.

J_2476.c: Colour woodblock print, Reading a letter by Suzuki Harunobu, printed in Japan between 1768 and 1770. Chūban format, nishiki-e print.

a: Shiba Kōkan, attributed to; Suzuki Harunobu, formerly attributed to
J_2477.c: Colour woodblock print representing a poem by Ono no Komachi from an untitled series of Six poetic immortals attributed to artist Shiba Kōkan, printed in Japan between 1770 and 1771. Chūban format, nishiki-e print. Although signed for Suzuki Harunobu, it is thought that this print is one of a small number of works created after his death by the artist Shiba Kōkan. Sometimes styled Suzuki Harunobu II, Kōkan later adopted the artist name Suzuki Harushige.

J_2478.t: Flower arrangements on a fine day (Ikebana no seiran)
J_2478.c: Colour woodblock print, 'Flower arrangements on a fine day' (Ikebana no seiran) from the series 'Eight newly-selected parlour views' (Shinsen zashiki hakkei) attributed to Kitao Masanobu, printed in Japan around 1780. Chūban format, nishiki-e print. A second print from this series, 'Returning sails of the hanging scroll' is preserved in the collections of the MFA (No. 21.5718).

J_2479.c: Colour woodblock print, 'Couple smoking together' possibly after Suzuki Harunobu, printed in Japan around 1770. Chūban format, nishiki-e print. An unsigned copy of this print in the collections of MFA Boston suggests that the work may not be by Suzuki Harunobu as signed. Following Harunobu's death in 1770, other artists are known to have produced work using his name.

J_2480.c: Colour woodblock print representing a poem by Minamoto no Kintada Ason from an untitled series of 36 immortal poets attributed to Suzuki Harunobu, printed in Japan between 1767 and 1768. Chūban format, nishiki-e print.

J_2481.c: Colour woodblock print, Mane'emon watching a couple possibly by or after Suzuki Harunobu, printed in Japan around 1770. Chūban format, nishiki-e print. This print appears to be related to more explicit erotic print albums documenting the voyeuristic adventures of Mane'emon. Shrunk to the size of a bean, Mane'emon observes various couples having sex, offering his own commentary from the sidelines.

J_2482.c: Colour woodblock print, 'Takigawa of the Ōgiya house' by Chōbunsai Eishi, published by Iwatoya Kisaburō in Edo (modern Tokyo), Japan, between 1795 and 1800. Ōban format, nishiki-e print.

J_2483.t: New Yoshiwara (Nii Yoshiwara) from Willow strands (Yanagi no ito)
J_2483.c: Colour woodblock print, 'New Yoshiwara' (Nii Yoshiwara) by Chōbunsai Eishi from the book 'Willow strands' (Yanagi no ito) published by Tsutaya Jūzaburō in Edo (modern Tokyo), Japan, in 1797. Page from a poetry anthology, nishiki-e print.

J_2484.c: Colour woodblock print, 'Poetry' (Waka) from the series 'Six arts in fashionable guise' (Fūzoku yatsushi rikugei) by Chōbunsai Eishi, published by Nishimuraya Yohachi in Edo (modern Tokyo), Japan, around 1794. Ōban format, nishiki-e print.

J_2485.c: Colour woodblock print, Couple boarding boat by Chōbunsai Eishi, published by Nishimuraya Yohachi in Edo (modern Tokyo), Japan, between 1785 and 1789. Ōban format diptych, nishiki-e print. Possibly once part of a triptych, only two sheets of this work are known.

J_2486.c: Colour woodblock print, Party under wisteria trellis by Chōbunsai Eishi, printed in Japan between 1785 and 1789. Aiban format diptych, nishiki-e print. Possibly once part of a triptych, only two sheets of this work are known.

J_2487.c: Colour woodblock print, Lovers in court robes attributed to Chōbunsai Eishi, printed in Japan around 1790. Chūban format, nishiki-e print. The intimate couple have been tentatively identified as poets Ariwara no Narihira and Ono no Komachi.

J_2488.c: Colour woodblock print, 'Suma' from the series 'Genji in fashionable modern guise' (Fūryū yatsushi Genji) by Chōbunsai Eishi, printed in Japan around 1789. Left sheet from a triptych, ōban format, nishiki-e print. This series of triptychs is noted for its muted colour palette.

J_2490.c: Colour woodblock print, Jurōjin from the series 'Treasures matched to lucky gods' (Fukujin takara awase) by Chōbunsai Eishi, published by Nishimuraya Yohachi in Edo (modern Tokyo), Japan, around 1795. Ōban format, nishiki-e print.

J_2491.t: Kasugano of the Kadotamaya house and Wakoku of the Echizenya house from Courtesans as the six immortal poets (Yūjo rokkasen)
J_2491.c: Colour woodblock print, 'Kasugano of the Kadotamaya house and Wakoku of the Echizenya house' from the triptych 'Courtesans as the six immortal poets' (Yūjo rokkasen) by Chōbunsai Eishi, published by Iwatoya Kisaburō in Edo (modern Tokyo), Japan, between 1790 and 1795. Centre sheet from a triptych, ōban format, nishiki-e print.

J_2492.c: Colour woodblock print, 'Hanaōgi of the Ōgiya house' from the series 'Beauties of the green houses as six floral immortals' (Seirō bijin rokkasen) by Chōbunsai Eishi, printed in Japan, around 1794. Ōban format, nishiki-e print. The Chester Beatty's impression of the print does not carry the censor seal or publisher's mark (of Nishimuraya Yohachi) found on other impressions of this print. The colouring of one of the woman's robes (here in black) also varies between these works.

J_2493.c: Colour woodblock print, 'Ten kinds of incense' (Jisshu kō) from the series 'Six arts in fashionable guise' (Fūzoku yatsushi rikugei) by Chōbunsai Eishi, published by Nishimuraya Yohachi in Edo (modern Tokyo), Japan, around 1794. Ōban format, nishiki-e print.

J_2494.c: Woodblock print of women in a mansion by Chōbunsai Eishi, published by Kōzuya Isuke; printed in ink and colours on paper in Japan, c. 1790. Possibly the left sheet of a triptych print.

J_2495.t: Representation of the coming of age ceremony of Lord Narihira (Narihira ason hatsu kanmuri yatsushi)
J_2495.c: Colour woodblock print, 'Representation of the coming of age ceremony of Lord Narihira' (Narihira ason hatsu kanmuri yatsushi) by Chōkōsai Eishō, published by Izumiya Ichibei in Edo (modern Tokyo), Japan, around 1797. Centre sheet from triptych, ōban format, nishiki-e print.

J_2496.c: Colour woodblock print, 'Komurasaki of the Kadotamaya house' from the untitled series Three gods of poetry by Chōkōsai Eishō, published by Yamaguchiya Chūsuke in Edo (modern Tokyo), Japan, around 1796. Ōban format, nishiki-e print.

J_2497.c: Colour woodblock print of lovers Osome and Hisamatsu from the series 'Mirror of beauties in jōruri roles' (Bijin awase jōruri kagami) by Ichirakutei Eisui, published by Maruya Bun'emon in Edo (modern Tokyo), Japan, around 1795. Ōban format, nishiki-e print.

J_2498.c: Colour woodblock print of lovers Shirai Gonpachi and Komurasaki from the series 'Mirror of beauties in jōruri roles' (Bijin awase jōruri kagami) by Ichirakutei Eisui, published by Maruya Bun'emon in Edo (modern Tokyo), Japan, around 1795. Ōban format, nishiki-e print.

J_2499.c: Colour woodblock print, 'Koto' from the series 'Musume Shigetada played by three instruments' (Sankyoku Musume Shigetada) by Keisai Eisen, published by Yamadaya Shōbei in Edo (modern Tokyo), Japan, between 1814 and 1822. Ōban format, nishiki-e print.

J_2500.t: Hara: Akashi of the Maru-Ebiya house
J_2500.c: Colour woodblock print, 'Hara: Akashi of the Maru-Ebiya house' from the series 'Game of courtesans on the road: Fifty-three pairings in the Yoshiwara' (Keisei dōchū sugoroku: Mitate Yoshiwara gojūsan tsui) by Keisai Eisen, published by Tsutaya Kichizō in Edo (modern Tokyo), Japan, in 1824 to 1825. Ōban format, nishiki-e print.

J_2501.t: Mishima: Tsukasa of the Ōgiya house
J_2501.c: Colour woodblock print, 'Mishima: Tsukasa of the Ōgiya house' from the series 'Game of courtesans on the road: Fifty-three pairings in the Yoshiwara' (Keisei dōchū sugoroku: Mitate Yoshiwara gojūsan tsui) by Keisai Eisen, published by Tsutaya Kichizō in Edo (modern Tokyo), Japan, in 1825 to 1826. Ōban format, nishiki-e print.

J_2502.t: Perspective view of theatre stage at Sakai-chō in Edo (Uki-e Edo Sakaichō shibai no zu)
J_2502.c: Colour woodblock print, 'Perspective view of theatre stage at Sakaichō in Edo' (Uki-e Edo Sakaichō shibai no zu) by Rekisentei Eiri, published by Izumiya Ichibei in Edo (modern Tokyo), Japan, between 1796 and 1801. Yoko-ōban format, nishiki-e print.

J_2503.c: Colour woodblock print, 'Uji' from the series 'Fashionable places for viewing fireflies' (Fūryū hotaru meisho awase no uchi) by Kikukawa Eizan, published by Yamaguchiya Tōbei in Edo (modern Tokyo), Japan, between 1811 and 1818. Ōban format, nishiki-e print.

J_2504.c: Colour woodblock print, 'Chōzan of the Chōjiya house' from the series 'Seven Komachi of the green houses' (Seirō nana Komachi) by Kikugawa Eizan, printed in Japan in 1806. Ōban format, nishiki-e print.

a: Kikukawa Eizan; Mikawaya Seiemon, probably by
J_2505.c: Colour woodblock print of women by brazier from the series 'Latest fashions of Fukagawa' (Tōfū michi no kakikara) by Kikukawa Eizan, probably published by Mikawaya Seiemon in Edo (modern Tokyo), Japan, around 1809. Ōban format, nishiki-e print.

J_2506.t: Woman holding falcon from Fashionable birds on the wrist (Fūryū kobushi no seichō)
J_2506.c: Colour woodblock print of woman holding falcon from the triptych 'Fashionable birds on the wrist' (Fūryū kobushi no seichō) by Kikukawa Eizan, published by an unidentified publisher known as Yama-sa in Edo (modern Tokyo), Japan, between 1804 and 1811. Right sheet from a triptych, ōban format, nishiki-e print.

J_2507.c: Colour woodblock print, 'Kamobuchi of the Ebiya house' from the series 'Trio of sake cups in the New Yoshiwara' (Shin Yoshiwara sansō no sakazuki) by Kikukawa Eizan, published by Izumiya Ichibei in edo (modern Tokyo), Japan, between 1818 and 1830. Ōban format, nishiki-e print.

J_2508.t: Tenth month: Autumn leaf viewing and festival of Ebisu (Nagatsuki, Momijigari, Ebisu-kō)
J_2508.c: Colour woodblock print, 'Tenth month: Autumn leaf viewing and festival of Ebisu' (Nagatsuki, Momijigari, Ebisu-kō) by Utagawa Toyoharu from an untitled series of Day and night scenes of twelve months, printed in Japan around 1773. Chūban format, nishiki-e print. This print, which shows activities of the tenth month, is one of a set of twelve similarly composed works designed by artists Utagawa Toyoharu, Kitao Shigemasa and and Katsukawa Shunshō. Each print in the series juxtaposes daytime and nighttime scenes appropriate to the month in question.

J_2509.t: Actor Sanogawa Ichimatsu II as Chūjō
J_2509.c: Colour woodblock print of actor Sanogawa Ichimatsu II as Chujo by Ippitsusai Bunchō, printed in Japan in 1769. Left sheet from a triptych, hosoban format, nishiki-e print. The triptych from which this print is taken shows actors performing in the play 'Edo no Hana Wakayagi Soga', performed at the Ichimura Theater in 1769. The play was written by Sakurada (1734-1806) and secured his reputation, establishing him as one of Edo's leading playwrights.

J_2510.t: Actors Arashi Sangorō II and Segawa Kikunojō II
J_2510.c: Colour woodblock print of actors Actors Arashi Sangorō II and Segawa Kikunojō II by Ippitsusai Bunchō, published by Maruya Jinpachi in Edo (modern Tokyo), Japan, in 1770. Hosoban format, nishiki-e print. This print shows a scene from the play 'Myōto-giku Izu no Kisewata', staged at the Ichimura Theatre in 1770. Arashi Sangorō II plays Minamoto no Yoritomo disguised as the hat-maker Daitarō, while Segawa Kikunojō II performs as Tatsu-hime disguised as the Snow Woman.

J_2511.t: Night rain in the Yoshiwara (Yoshiwara no yoru no ame)
J_2511.c: Colour woodblock print, 'Night rain in the Yoshiwara' (Yoshiwara no yoru no ame) from the series 'Eight views of Azuma' (Azuma Hakkei) by Ippitsusai Bunchō, printed in Japan between 1772 and 1781. Chūban format, nishiki-e print.

J_2512.t: Actor Ichikawa Yaozō II as the fox Sakon
J_2512.c: Colour woodblock print of actor Ichikawa Yaozō II as the fox Sakon by Ippitsusai Bunchō, published by Maruya Jinpachi in Edo (modern Tokyo), Japan, in 1770. Hosoban format, nishiki-e print. The print takes as its subject a scene from the play 'Forest of the Nue monster: Target of the eleventh month' (Nue no mori ichiyō no mato) performed at the Nakamura-za theatre in 1770.

J_2513.c: Colour woodblock print, 'Fifth month: Catching fireflies' (Gogatsu hotarugari) from an untitled series of Twelve months of children's games by Kitao Shigemasa, printed in Japan between 1770 and 1775. Chūban format, nishiki-e print.

J_2514.c: Colour woodblock print of mother holding child from the series 'Twelve costumes of beauties' (Bijin jūni hitoe) by Chōbunsai Eishi, published by Izumiya Ichibei in Edo (modern Tokyo), Japan, around 1799. Koban format, nishiki-e print.

J_2515.c: Colour woodblock print, 'Green pavilion' (Seirō) from the series 'Amuseuments of five colours' (Goshiki no asobi) by Chōbunsai Eishi, published by Nishimuraya Yohachi in Edo (modern Tokyo), Japan, around 1787. Chūban format, nishiki-e print.

a: Katsukawa Shunchō, possibly by; Fushimiya Zenroku
J_2516.c: Colour woodblock print of Evening at the riverbank, possibly by Katsukawa Shunchō, published by Fushimiya Zenroku in Edo (modern Tokyo), Japan, around 1785. Chūban format, nishiki-e print.

J_2517.c: Colour woodblock print, 'Komurasaki of the Tamaya' from the series 'Mirror of beauties of the green pavilions' (Seirō bijin kagami) by Ichirakutei Eisui, published by Maruya Bun'emon in Edo (modern Tokyo), Japan, between 1795 and 1801. Aiban format, nishiki-e print.

J_2518.c: Colour woodblock print of the poet Busata Noriuchi of Biyō by Eishōsai Chōki, published by Tsutaya Jūzaburō in Edo (modern Tokyo), Japan, between 1789 and 1801. Chūban format, nishiki-e print.

J_2519.t: Yaoya Hanbei and his wife Ochiyo (Yaoya Hanbei Ochiyo)
J_2519.c: Colour woodblock print, 'Yaoya Hanbei and his wife Ochiyo' (Yaoya Hanbei Ochiyo) by Eishōsai Chōki, published by an unidentified publisher known as Maru-ta, between 1795 and 1801. Chūban format, nishiki-e print.

J_2520.c: Colour woodblock print, 'Shinowara of the Tsuruya' from the series 'Courtesans as seven Komachi' (Yūkun nana Komachi) by Kitagawa Utamaro, published by Izumiya Ichibei in Edo (modern Tokyo), Japan, around 1805. Ōban format, nishiki-e print.

J_2521.c: Colour woodblock print, 'Act 10' (Jūdanme) from the series 'Treasury of loyal retainers' (Chūshingura) by Kitagawa Utamaro, published by Nishimuraya Yohachi in Edo (modern Tokyo), Japan, around 1801. Ōban format, nishiki-e print.

J_2522.t: Newly published perspective view: Enjoying cool evening at Edo's Ryōgoku bridge (Shinpan uki-e Edo Ryōgokubashi suzumi no zu)
J_2522.c: Colour woodblock print, 'Newly published perspective view: Enjoying cool evening at Edo's Ryōgoku bridge' (Shinpan uki-e Edo Ryōgokubashi suzumi no zu) by Kitagawa Utamaro II, published by Yamaguchiya Tōbei in Edo (modern Tokyo), Japan, between 1806 and 1818. Yoko-ōban format, nishiki-e print.

J_2523.t: Hunter (Karyūdo) from Spring amusements: fox game (Shunkyō mitate kitsune ken)
J_2523.c: Colour woodblock print, 'Hunter' (Karyūdo) from the triptych 'Spring amusements: fox game' (Shunkyō mitate kitsune ken) by Kitagawa Utamaro, published by Murataya Jirōbei in Edo (modern Tokyo), Japan, between 1801 and 1804. Left sheet from a triptych, ōban format, nishiki-e print. The fox game is similar to rock-paper-scissors. While the hunter (represented here by a woman holding a handscroll as if it were a weapon) can defeat the fox, the fox triumphs over the village head who out-ranks the hunter. The Chester Beatty has the right and left prints from this triptych, the fox and the hunter, though background details suggest that they may be from different editions. In the complete triptych, the village head, depicted as an elegant young man, sits between the fox and the hunter.

J_2524.t: Fox (Kitsune) from Spring amusements: fox game (Shunkyō mitate kitsune ken)
J_2524.c: Colour woodblock print, 'Fox' (Kitsune) from the triptych 'Spring amusements: fox game' (Shunkyō mitate kitsune ken) by Kitagawa Utamaro, published by Murataya Jirōbei in Edo (modern Tokyo), Japan, between 1801 and 1804. Right sheet from a triptych, ōban format, nishiki-e print. The fox game is similar to rock-paper-scissors. While the fox (represented here by a woman playing with a ball) triumphs over the village head, the village head out-ranks the hunter who defeats the fox. The Chester Beatty has the right and left prints from this triptych, the fox and the hunter, though background details suggest that they may be from different editions. In the complete triptych, the village head, depicted as an elegant young man, sits between the fox and the hunter.

J_2525.c: Colour woodblock print, Catching fireflies by Kitagawa Utamaro, published by Izumiya Ichibei in Edo (modern Tokyo), Japan, around 1796. Centre sheet from a triptych, ōban format, nishiki-e print.

J_2526.c: Colour woodblock print, Tomimoto Toyohina from the series 'Renowned beauties likened to six immortal poets' (Kōmei bijin rokkasen) by Kitagawa Utamaro, published by Ōmiya Gonkurō in Edo (modern Tokyo), Japan, around 1795. Ōban format, nishiki-e print.

J_2527.t: Tears of union between Ochiyo and Hanbei (Ochiyo Hanbei no yoru no ame)
J_2527.c: Colour woodblock print, 'Tears of union between Ochiyo and Hanbei' (Ochiyo Hanbei no yoru no ame) from the series 'Eight pledges at lovers' meetings' (Ōmi hakkei) by Kitagawa Utamaro, published by Ōmiya Gonkurō in Edo (modern Tokyo), Japan, around 1798. Ōban format, nishiki-e print.

J_2528.t: Couple smoking in front of screen
J_2528.c: Colour woodblock print, 'Couple smoking in front of screen' by Kitagawa Utamaro, printed in Japan around 1804. Ōban format, nishiki-e print. Although there is no signature on this print, other surviving impressions sometimes carry either Utamaro's signature or both Utamaro's signature and the seal of publisher Iwatoya Kisaburō.

J_2529.c: Woodblock print, Shōki umpires wrestling demons by Kitagawa Utamaro, printed in Japan in the late eighteenth century. Ōban format print.

J_2530.t: Yamauba and Kintarō at New Year
J_2530.c: Colour woodblock print of Yamauba and Kintarō at New Year by Kitagawa Utamaro, published by Nishimuraya Yohachi in Edo (modern Tokyo), Japan, between 1801 and 1804. Ōban format, nishiki-e print.

J_2531.c: Colour woodblock print, Weaver from the series 'Twelve types of women's handicraft' (Fujin tewaza jūni kō) by Kitagawa Utamaro, published by Wakasaya Yoichi in Edo (modern tokyo), Japan, around 1798. Ōban format, nishiki-e print.

J_2532.t: Fish market at Shiba beach (Shibaura uo ichi no zu)
J_2532.c: Colour woodblock print, 'Fish market at Shiba beach' (Shibaura uo ichi no zu) by Kitagawa Utamaro II, published by Ōmiya Gonkurō in Edo (modern Tokyo), Japan, dated 1807. Right sheet from a triptych, ōban format, nishiki-e print.

J_2533.t: Hour of the hare: Servant women (U no koku gejo)
J_2533.c: Colour woodblock print, 'Hour of the hare: Servant women' (U no koku gejo) from the series 'Customs of beauties around the clock' (Fūzoku bijin tokei) by Kitagawa Utamaro, published by Izumiya Ichibei in Edo (modern Tokyo), Japan, around 1798. Ōban format, nishiki-e print.

J_2534.t: Evening view of Naka-no-chō in the New Yoshiwara (Shin Yoshiwara Naka no chō yūkei no zu)
J_2534.c: Colour woodblock print, 'Evening view of Naka-no-chō in the New Yoshiwara' (Shin Yoshiwara Naka no chō yūkei no zu) from the series 'Perspective prints of Edo' (Edo uki-e) by Kitagawa Utamaro II, published by Yamaguchiya Tōbei in Edo (modern Tokyo), Japan, between 1806 and 1818. Yoko-ōban format, nishiki-e print.

J_2535.t: Women feeding bird from Men's stamping dance (Otoko tōka)
J_2535.c: Colour woodblock print of women feeding bird by Kitagawa Utamaro from the book 'Men's stamping dance' (Otoko tōka) published by Tsutaya Jūzaburō in Edo (modern Tokyo), Japan, in 1798. Page from a poetry anthology, nishiki-e print.

J_2536.c: Colour woodblock print, 'Act 2' (Nidanme) from the series 'Treasury of loyal retainers' (Chūshingura) by Kitagawa Utamaro, published by Nishimuraya Yohachi in Edo (modern Tokyo), Japan, around 1801. Ōban format, nishiki-e print.

J_2537.c: Colour woodblock print, 'Fujiwara no Ietaka' (Jūnii Ietaka) from the series 'Newly-compiled anthology' (Shin shūi shū) by Kitagawa Utamaro, published by Izumiya Ichibei in Edo (modern Tokyo), Japan, in 1800. Aiban format, nishiki-e print.

J_2538.c: Triptych colour woodblock print, ‘Drying clothes’ by Kitagawa Utamaro, published by Iwatoya Kisaburō in Edo (modern Tokyo), Japan, around 1790. A group of women dry clothes on a rooftop platform overlooking the city with Mt. Fuji’s distinctive peak visible in the distance. While the child reaches up for attention, the cat steals over the balustrade. As the cat seeks its prey among the pine tree’s branches, it fails to notice the cuckoo flying overhead.

J_2541.c: Colour woodblock print, 'Gullible type' (Shōjiki mono) from the series 'A parent's moralising spectacles' (Kyōkun oya no megane) by Kitagawa Utamaro, published by Tsuruya Kinsuke in Edo (modern Tokyo), Japan, around 1802. Ōban format, nishiki-e print.

J_2542.t: Elegant treasure boat of children (Fūryū kodakarabune)
J_2542.c: Colour woodblock print, 'Elegant treasure boat of children' (Fūryū kodakarabune) by Kitagawa Utamaro, published by Murataya Jirōbei in Edo (modern Tokyo), Japan, dated 1805. Right sheet from a triptych, ōban format, nishiki-e print.

J_2543.t: Wedding of the fox Tamahime (Tamahime kitsune no yomeiri)
J_2543.c: Colour woodblock print, 'Wedding of the fox Tamahime' (Tamahime kitsune no yomeiri) from the series 'Niwaka festival entertainments in the Yoshiwara in full swing' (Seirō Niwaka zensei asobi) by Kitagawa Utamaro, published by Sumimaruya Jinsuke in Edo (modern Tokyo), Japan, between 1801 and 1804. Aiban format, nishiki-e print.

J_2544.c: Colour woodblock print, 'Haruyama of the Matsubaya house' from a pentaptych of women of the Matsubaya as musicians by Kitagawa Utamaro, published by Maruya Bun'emon in Edo (modern Tokyo), Japan, around 1797. Sheet from a pentaptych, ōban format, nishiki-e print.

J_2545.c: Colour woodblock print, 'Act 1' (Shodan) from the series 'Treasury of loyal retainers' (Chūshingura) by Kitagawa Utamaro, published by Nishimuraya Yohachi in Edo (modern Tokyo), Japan, around 1801. Ōban format, nishiki-e print.

J_2546.c: Colour woodblock print, 'Act 8' (Hachidanme) from the series 'Treasury of loyal retainers' (Chūshingura) by Kitagawa Utamaro, published by Nishimuraya Yohachi in Edo (modern Tokyo), Japan, around 1801. Ōban format, nishiki-e print.

J_2547.c: Colour woodblock print, 'Act 11' (Jūichidanme) from the series 'Treasury of loyal retainers' (Chūshingura) by Kitagawa Utamaro, published by Nishimuraya Yohachi in Edo (modern Tokyo), Japan, around 1801. Ōban format, nishiki-e print.

J_2548.c: Colour woodblock print, 'Act 9' (Kudanme) from the series 'Treasury of loyal retainers' (Chūshingura) by Kitagawa Utamaro, published by Nishimuraya Yohachi in Edo (modern Tokyo), Japan, around 1801. Ōban format, nishiki-e print.

J_2553.c: Colour woodblock print, Morning parting by Kitagawa Utamaro, published by Moriya Jihei in Edo (modern Tokyo), Japan, in 1800. Left sheet from a triptych, ōban format, nishiki-e print. With the gate of Mimeguri Shrine visible across the Sumida River in the background, this scene of clients returning home is not taken from Edo's regulated brothel district - the Yoshiwara - but rather the Yama no Shuku area. When fires ravaged the Yoshiwara, brothel keepers would petition for the district to have 'temporary lodgings' elsewhere. The lodgings shown here likely relate to a fire that swept through the Yoshiwara in the spring of 1800.

J_2588.c: Colour woodblock print, Kumagai Jirō Naozane cut from ‘Fujieda’ by Utagawa Kuniyoshi from the series '53 pairings along the Tōkaidō road' (Tōkaidō gojūsan tsui), presumably published by Ibaya Senzaburō in Edo (modern Tokyo), Japan, in 1845. Heavily trimmed ōban format, nishiki-e print. Fujieda was the hometown of twelfth-century warrior turned priest, Kumagai Jirō Naozane. J_2590.c: Colour woodblock print, 'Guo Ju' (Kakkyo) from the series 'Mirror of 24 paragons of filial piety for children' (Nijūshi kō dōji kagami) by Utagawa Kuniyoshi, published by Wakasaya Yoichi in Edo (modern Tokyo), Japan, around 1843. Yoko-ōban format, nishiki-e print. Originally compiled during China’s Yuan dynasty (1280-1368), the suite of stories ‘24 paragons of filial piety’ presents examples of children showing proper regard for their parents in line with Confucian ideals. The stories also found popularity in Japan. Seeing his aged mother weakened by hunger, Guo Ju (known as Kakkyo in Japan) prepared to kill his child that there might be one less mouth to feed. While digging a grave in preparation, he discovered a pot of gold and the child’s life was spared.

Yoko-ōban format, nishiki-e print. Originally compiled during China’s Yuan dynasty (1280-1368), the suite of stories ‘24 paragons of filial piety’ presents examples of children showing proper regard for their parents in line with Confucian ideals. The stories also found popularity in Japan. Wu Meng (Japanese: Gomō) allowed himself to be bitten by hungry mosquitoes that they would spare his sleeping parents.

J_2656.t: Kaminarimon gate at Kannon temple, Asakusa (Asakusa Kanzeon kaminarimon no zu)
J_2656.c: Colour woodblock print, 'Kaminarimon gate at Kannon temple, Asakusa' (Asakusa Kanzeon kaminarimon no zu) by Tamagawa Shūchō, published by Wakasaya Yoichi in Edo (modern Tokyo), Japan, around 1795. Yoko-ōban format, nishiki-e print. The famous Kaminarimon gate of Asakusa’s Sensōji Kannon temple is flanked by the gods of wind (right) and thunder (left). Unusually for a Japanese print of this type, Tamagawa Shūchō has included cropped figures in the foreground increasing the sense of crowds bustling around the temple.

Mon_1953_1.c: Wooden cover from Great Liberation sutra, made in Beijing, China after 1708. Colours and gold on wood with silk panels. Wooden covers protected sacred manuscripts from damage and were often decorated with finely carved or painted figures and decorative motifs. Images of the Buddha and his disciples are painted on the front cover in colours and gold, and the Guardians of the Four Quarters are painted on the back cover in colours and gold.

Pap_1011.c: Christian amulet or magical text written in Greek on papyrus and made in Egypt probably in the 4th century. The horizontal breakage at regular intervals suggests the sheet was once folded or rolled. The amulet is composed of a serpent (or dragon) eating its own tail (οὐροβόρος) encircling an open bookroll filled with an eight-by-eight grid of Greek vowels. A bird at the top left holds a christogram (⳩) in its beak. The text on the serpent is a common magical palindrome, the final letters being ιαεω, the Greek magical rendering of the name Yaweh (with an additional letter). A tabula ansata (tablet with handles) hangs off the bottom of the serpent. The whole is surrounded by short names and phrases.

Per_104_1.t: Hushang kills the Black Div (recto) and Hushang discovers fire while killing a dragon with a stone (verso), from the Book of Kings (Shahnama) by Firdausi
Per_104_1.c: Hushang kills the Black Div (recto) and Hushang discovers fire while killing a dragon with a stone (verso), folio from the Book of Kings (Shahnama) of Firdausi. Detached folio, ink, pigments and gold on paper, Persian text with three chapter-headings and two paintings, probably Tabriz, Iran, c. 1300. This folio is from a dispersed manuscript known to scholars as the "First Small Shahnama", of which seventy-seven folios are now in the Chester Beatty. The "Small Shahnama" manuscripts are the earliest known illustrated examples of the Book of Kings (Shahnama), the epic Persian poem composed c. 1010 by Firdausi. Two manuscripts are dispersed, and a third is in the Freer Gallery in Washington, DC. Of small format, these three manuscripts are undated, but usually attributed to c. 1300 on stylistic grounds. Details of iconography confirm that production was after the Mongol invasions of Iran and Iraq, and the establishment of Ilkhanid rule in 1258.
